note: What to show depending on the audience. All matching rules apply, not only the most specific one.

show: The classical test or model and its non-parametric alternative
The assumptions of the model and how you checked them (residual plots, tests)
The interpretation of each main estimate in one sentence
avoid: Reporting only the p-value, without the estimate and its confidence interval

show: Estimates in clinical units, with confidence intervals
avoid: The full table of model coefficients

show: The absolute risk in each group, as natural frequencies (for example 12 in 100)
The risk difference and the number needed to treat (NNT)
The risk ratio if the outcome is common
avoid: Presenting the odds ratio as if it were a risk ratio
The relative risk reduction alone: it looks larger than the absolute one

show: Survival or cumulative incidence curves with the number at risk
The absolute risk at a fixed clinical time (for example at 5 years) by group
The RMST: mean event-free time gained within a fixed horizon
Rates by group (for example events per 100 patient-years) alongside the rate ratio
The predicted probability of each category by group, alongside the common odds ratio
The reporting guideline for the study design, with the completed checklist
Estimates with confidence intervals; exact p-values, not only < 0.05
Methods described well enough to be replicated: software, versions, handling of missing data
avoid: Claiming no effect from a non-significant p-value

show: The DAG or the criteria used to choose the confounders
Only the effect of the exposure in the main table
avoid: Interpreting the coefficients of the covariates (Table 2 fallacy)

show: The full model equation, so that others can validate it externally
